newsitem.title: USA: Maine Yankee, Entergy approve management contract.
newsitem.headline: Maine Yankee, Entergy approve management contract.

text.p: Maine Yankee and Entergy Nuclear Inc Thursday signed an interim contract for Entergy to manage the troubled nuclear facility until Sept. 30, the companies announced.

Officials said the companies would now negotiate a "longer term" contact for Entergy to oversee operations at the plant - which has had related safety-related shutdowns and is under close watch by federal regulators.

The cost of the agreement was not disclosed. The short-term agreement calls for Entergy to be paid a retainer for services. Officials said the longer-term agreement will likely include performance incentives.

Nuclear Regulatory Commission officials have said they will review the contracts to see if it requires any modifications of Maine Yankee's operating license. The management agreement is the first of its kind in the U.S. nuclear industry.
The contract makes effective Mike Sellman's selection as Maine Yankee's president. Sellman, an Entergy Vice President, assumed the post this month. He told reporters he remains an Entergy employee.
Sellman will work at Maine Yankee with between eight and 10 senior members of Energy's staff, the companies said.

The 910-megawatt plant has been subjected to repeated shutdowns and regulatory inspections for the past two years. The facility is currently off-line to fix misrouted electrical cables and faulty fuel rods.

Maine Yankee is 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power Co, 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities, seven percent by Bangor Hydro, five percent by Maine Public Service Co. and 10 percent by other New England utilities.
